This confirms a bitemporal gap: the Q2 unit cost invoice (J00016, effective 2026-04-01) was not entered into the books until 2026-04-06, five days after it took effect.

- As of 2026-04-03 (using only records entered by that date), the books' most recent applicable cost for the insulated bottle (item A-100) on 2026-04-02 was still $15.00, from J00013 (Meridian Q1 2026 invoice, effective 2026-01-01, entered 2026-01-06).
- Looking at the books now (2026-09-29), the record that applies to 2026-04-02 is J00016, the Meridian Q2 2026 invoice: unit cost $18.00, effective 2026-04-01, entered 2026-04-06.

So the $3.00 (20%) jump was on the books all along as of 2026-04-01 effective date, but hadn't been keyed in yet as of 2026-04-03, meaning anyone querying the books on 2026-04-03 would have seen the stale $15.00 figure for a day that, as of today, is booked at $18.00.

ANSWER: As of 2026-04-03, the books still showed the insulated bottle's unit cost applying on 2026-04-02 as $15.00 (the Q1 2026 Meridian rate, entered 2026-01-06), because the Q2 rate hadn't been keyed in yet. Looking at the books now, that same day, 2026-04-02, is booked at $18.00 (the Q2 2026 Meridian rate, effective 2026-04-01, entered 2026-04-06).
